title: Phase 5 · Observe: See What Is Happening in Production
html:
Goal: going live is not the finish line. In this chapter you use the V3 console's observability dashboard, session replay and trace waterfall to find where an answer spent its time and how many tokens it burned. Then you use the Standards workbench's drift watch to re-apply the signed standard to lab-service-assistant on a schedule, and read the scorecard and decision history to answer "is the standard still holding, and who decided what".

Prerequisites

You need From
Release policy of workspace default set to gated (every invoke goes to the live endpoint) The Roles chapter
Criteria unicorn-service-criteria v1 (P1, P2, K1, C1, Q1, S1, S2) published and signed by biz-owner; golden set unicorn-service-golden serving it, curated 24 / 15 / 9 with holdout sealed The Define and Evaluate chapters
Deployed lab-service-assistant (with knowledge base lab-unicorn-policies) and lab-policy-advisor The Build chapter
The release gate has run on a candidate; S2 has a calibration decision (in this lab "not aligned") The Evaluate chapter
live of lab-service-assistant points at the released version N+1 (teams that skipped the re-release stay on the old version — this chapter works either way); Cedar policies on launchpad-gw switched to ENFORCE; API key console-1 The Release chapter

Accounts used in this chapter, and why:

Account Does Why
developer Generates test traffic, reads traces, configures and triggers the drift watch Editing the watch needs criteria.manage, triggering a run needs eval.run — engineering work
biz-owner Reads the dashboard, sessions, intent view and scorecard The business owner checks whether the standard holds but does not change schedules; in a fresh window their rail shows the everyday modules only
admin Reads spend & alerts, Gateway decision logs and the decision history GET /api/costs and GET /api/audit are admin-only (spend by person names individuals)

Observability data comes from CloudWatch Transaction Search (aws/spans). Spans land with a delay (in this lab the last answer's trace was still incomplete 10 seconds after it finished and fully visible 2.5 minutes later), so a trace you cannot see right after chatting is normal. Dashboard queries are cached for 60 seconds per (view, range); the right of the page header shows "cached Ns ago", and Refresh next to it forces a re-read.

1. Generate a little traffic

Sign in as developer, click Chat at the top of the rail (/v3/chat), pick lab-service-assistant in the Agent picker in the left column, click New conversation and send the questions below one at a time (wait for each answer):

text
I bought Bluetooth earbuds on Unicorn Mall and signed for them the day before yesterday. The box is open but the device is not activated. Can I still use the 7-day no-reason return?
I'm a Gold member and the order paid amount was ¥380. How soon do I get my refund after returning it?
Unicorn Air UC1208, Standard economy, fare ¥1,200, departing in three days. How much do I get back if I refund now?
Does Economy Lite include free checked baggage?
Unicorn Hotels Standard Prepaid rate, check-in 20 October, I cancel on 19 October at 10:00. How much is charged?

Switch the Agent picker to lab-policy-advisor (switching starts a new conversation) and send:

text
Can a flash-sale item use a platform coupon? Does the spend-threshold discount still stack?

Expected result: both agents answer; a tool row appears above each answer (kb_search for lab-service-assistant, skills and lab-unicorn-policies-…___Retrieve for lab-policy-advisor), and every answer has two icon buttons, thumbs up / down (their labels are Good answer / Bad answer). Do not thumbs-down yet — the Feed back chapter uses it. With live = v4 the answers cite policy rule ids (teams that skipped 1.6 of the Release chapter and stayed on v2 get no ids).

One observed answer per question (live = v4, model GLM-5.3; the chat time is from send to the end of the answer on the Chat page, the trace figures come from the session detail in sections 3 and 4):

Question Key points of one observed answer Chat time Trace duration · spans · LLM · tokens · cost
Opened, unactivated earbuds Within the window (R-01); electronics qualify for the 7-day no-reason return only with an intact factory seal and no activation (R-03): only the outer box opened and the seal intact → still returnable, factory seal broken → not; quality issues can still be returned within 15 days (R-04); it ends by asking whether the factory seal is intact 13.4 s 8.3 s · 19 · 2 · 1,682 · ≈$0.010
Gold member, ¥380 order Instant refund at pickup (R-07); wallet within 2 hours, debit card 1–3 working days, credit card 3–7 working days (R-08) 5.2 s 4.5 s · 12 · 1 · 715 · ≈$0.004
UC1208 Standard economy refund Fee 25% = ¥300 (A-03), taxes ¥80 refunded in full (A-06), you get ¥980 (A-07) 8.7 s 8.1 s · 19 · 2 · 1,268 · ≈$0.007
Economy Lite checked baggage 0 kg free checked allowance (A-12); this observed answer then gave the ¥20/kg excess rate and the 32 kg / 100 × 60 × 40 cm piece limits (A-15) instead of the ¥120 / 20 kg purchase price (A-14) 4.6 s 3.9 s · 12 · 1 · 449 · ≈$0.003
Standard Prepaid, cancel 19 Oct 10:00 28 hours before check-in, under 48 hours, first night charged (H-03), with the official ¥680/night example (H-10) 11.9 s 11 s · 17 · 2 · 1,580 · ≈$0.009
Flash sale and platform coupon (lab-policy-advisor) Flash-sale items cannot use a platform coupon (R-11); the spend-threshold discount still stacks (R-10, R-11); this observed answer came back in Chinese 12.9 s 12 s · 39 · 3 · 1,264 · ≈$0.007

These are the readings of one run in this lab: each answer's trace took 3.9–12 seconds and 449–1,682 tokens, and every one cost less than a cent.

V3's Chat page holds only the conversation, with no trace panel. Read the spans of these sessions under Observability → Sessions below; Open in chat on the session detail takes you back to Chat to continue the session.

2. Read the dashboard

In another browser window (a private window or another browser profile) sign in as biz-owner. In a fresh window a member account's rail shows the everyday modules only: the fixed entries at the top — Command center, Agents, Chat, Release gate — stay, and Modules keeps only Architect assistant, New agent, Knowledge Bases, Releases, Issue box, Observability, Intent view, Standards, Video introductions. Show every module at the bottom of Modules shows them all; it is a view filter, not authorization.

Click rail Modules → Agent runtime → Observability (/v3/observability); the Dashboard tab opens. Leave the time range to the right of the tabs at 24H (also: 1H, 6H, 7D).

In the image: 1 range 24H; 2 Needs a look: "P95 latency is 20s"; 3 the tiles Traces 157, Sessions 139, Error rate 0.0%, Latency P50 / P95 5.6s / 20s, Tokens 246K (≈$1.08); 4 the Traffic and Latency charts (latency peak 23s); 5 Tools (kb_search 175 calls and others) and Tokens by model (prices updated 2026-10-10).

Area How to read it
Needs a look The page leads with what stands out (a high error rate, an error spike, a slow P95, a failing tool); click one to jump to the matching traces. When nothing does it says "Nothing stands out across N traces." and the page title reads "Running clean"
Traces One invoke is one trace; the line below splits ok and failed
Sessions Sessions in range, plus the number of active agents
Error rate Turns red above 5%
Latency P50 / P95 Percentiles of the root span; many short requests pull them down
Tokens Total tokens, with input / output tokens and a ≈$ cost estimate below
Traffic Traces per bucket, errors on top
Latency Root-span P50 and P95 curves
Tools Calls and success rate per tool, failing first: kb_search / kb_deep_search of lab-service-assistant (generated code calling Bedrock retrieval on lab-unicorn-policies directly) and …___Retrieve of lab-policy-advisor (knowledge base gateway tool)
Tokens (chart) Tokens and estimated cost per model; cost comes from a price map, not your bill

On cost: the bottom of the Tokens chart card names the price map (here price map: config/launchpad.yaml · model_prices · prices updated 2026-10-10). The map has global.zai.glm-5.3 (input 1.68, output 5.28 USD per million tokens), so GLM-5.3 cost shows as a ≈$ amount; a model missing from it shows tokens and — for cost. Update prices at the top right of that card rewrites the price map shared by the whole console — the administrator does that.

Expected result (measured in this lab, 24H):

  • The page title is 1 thing worth a look; Needs a look has 1 item: "P95 latency is 20s", with "Slow above 10s; a root span past 30s counts as a timeout." and a Traces link on the right.
  • Traces 157 (157 ok · 0 failed); Sessions 139 (9 active agents); Error rate 0.0% (0 of 157 traces); Latency P50 / P95 5.6s / 20s; Tokens 246K (in 92K · out 154K · ≈$1.08).
  • The Traffic chart shows traces per bucket; the Latency chart reads "peak 23s" with the legend P50 · 5.6s and P95 · 20s. P95 is far above section 1's single answers because the 24 hours also hold earlier chapters' evaluation runs and the BYOC and canary calls.
  • Tools: kb_search 175 calls, calculator 21, lab-unicorn-policies-seyvaxgxng___Retrieve 12, kb_deep_search 6, skills 5, current_utc_time 3, all at 100%.
  • Tokens chart: global.zai.glm-5.3 206K · ≈$0.980, global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5 41K · ≈$0.099.

3. Replay a session

Switch to the Sessions tab. Filter the agent picker (default All agents) to lab-service-assistant; the filter next to it offers All / With errors / Clean, and Search a session id narrows further. Each row shows Session, Agent, Traces, LLM calls, Tokens · cost, Errors and Last active. After filtering, the first row (most recent Last active) is the five-question session from section 1: in this lab Traces 5, LLM calls 8, Tokens · cost 5,694 / ≈$0.033. Click it to open the session detail; its Conversation block starts with the user message "I bought Bluetooth earbuds on Unicorn Mall…".

In the image: 1 Open in chat, Score now and refresh; 2 tiles: Traces 5, LLM calls 8, Tokens 5,694 (in 16 · out 5,678), Est. cost ≈$0.033; 3 the Conversation replay (actor developer); 4 Traces in this session: five POST /invocations cards, the top one (11s) is the slowest.

The session detail has:

  • Header: the title is the agent name, the small line above it Session · <Session ID>, and below it the first-seen / last times. On the right: Open in chat (continues this session in Chat), Score now and a refresh button.
  • Tiles: Traces (with Copy id for the full Session ID), LLM calls, Tokens (in / out), Est. cost.
  • Conversation: turn-by-turn replay; the small line at its top right names the source (here agentcore memory · ListEvents · actor developer).
  • Traces in this session: one card per invoke with duration, spans, LLM calls, tokens and cost (here, newest first: 11s, 3.9s, 8.1s, 4.5s, 8.3s). The card title is the root operation, POST /invocations. A multi-turn session has several cards — read them one by one rather than taking the session total as one answer's cost.
  • Online evaluation: appears only when the agent has an online evaluation config (the Feed back chapter), with the evaluators' scores; with a config but no score yet it says "No online evaluation scored this session yet.". No online evaluation is configured at this point, so the block does not appear.
  • Score now: V3 has not rebuilt this; the button opens this session's full page inside V3 (address /v2/observability?…&full=1), with the Score now card further down.

Score now (developer):

  1. As developer, open the same session detail, click Score now and scroll to the Score now card (its title reads "0 of 5 evaluators selected"; the evaluator list has 35 entries over 4 pages).
  2. Type Helpfulness into the search box at the top right of the card and tick Helpfulness (Builtin.Helpfulness); then type privacy and tick unicorn_privacy_guard. Both judge the session alone and need no expected answer. unicorn_fee_check and unicorn_no_overpromise can be ticked too, but their rubrics reference {expected_response}, which a session does not have, so leave them out. Only Builtin.TrajectoryExactOrderMatch, Builtin.TrajectoryInOrderMatch and Builtin.TrajectoryAnyOrderMatch cannot be ticked; hovering shows "Needs ground truth — not available for on-demand session scoring" (/api/eval/evaluators returns requires_ground_truth for those three only).
  3. Click Score at the top right of the card; the "Score this session now?" dialog says "Runs 2 evaluator(s) over this session's spans — one billable judge inference per evaluator. Results are shown here and not persisted."; click Score in the dialog.

In the image: 1 the two picked evaluators; 2 the Score button; 3 the summary "105 spans sent · 10 results · not persisted"; 4 the results: each evaluator scores each of the 5 traces once, Builtin.Helpfulness 0.83 / 1.00, unicorn_privacy_guard pass on all.

Expected result (measured in this lab, back in 24 seconds): below the card appear "105 spans sent · 10 results · not persisted" and a results table with columns Evaluator, Score, Label, Explanation — click row to expand, Tokens (in / out) and Status (all Scored). Both are trace-level evaluators, so each scores each of the 5 traces once: Builtin.Helpfulness in one observed run gave 0.83 / 0.83 / 1.00 / 0.83 / 0.83 (in question order; 1.00 is labelled Above And Beyond, 0.83 Very Helpful), and unicorn_privacy_guard gave 1.00 with label pass on all five (its explanations came back in Chinese); the judge input per result was 5,465–14,262 tokens. Results are not persisted; for a stored, repeatable score use an evaluation run on the golden set.

Score now makes billed Bedrock calls and the route is open to every member. Following this workshop's split of duties, let developer press Score; biz-owner only reads.

4. Find the slow call in the trace waterfall

Back in biz-owner's session detail, under Traces in this session, click the card with the longest duration (each card reads duration · N spans · N LLM · N tokens · cost; compare the first number; in this lab it is the top card, 11s · 17 spans · 2 LLM · 1,580 tokens · ≈$0.009, the hotel cancellation question); or on the Observability page switch to the Traces tab and click the same trace.

In the image: 1 tiles: Duration 11s, Spans / LLM 17 / 2, Tokens 1,580, Est. cost ≈$0.009; 2 legend: LLM, Tool, Memory, HTTP, Agent; 3 the tool row kb_search (444ms); 4 the second model call chat global.zai.glm-5.3 (5.8s, the bulk of the time); 5 the Span card: model, finish reason, duration and tokens (output 905 · ≈$0.005).

The header title is the root operation with its status (here POST /invocations · OK), and the small line below gives agent, start time and service name; Open session on the right goes back to the session. The tiles are Duration (with Copy id), Spans / LLM, Tokens and Est. cost. The Waterfall colours spans by LLM / Tool / Memory / Gateway / HTTP / Agent / Other, and the legend lists only the categories this trace has (here LLM, Tool, Memory, HTTP, Agent); a tool span's row shows the tool name (kb_search; the full span name is execute_tool kb_search). The structure of this trace in this lab (durations on the right):

text
POST /invocations                              11s
├─ Bedrock AgentCore.ListEvents ×3             61–85ms     ← read short-term memory
├─ Bedrock AgentCore.RetrieveMemoryRecords ×2  256–301ms   ← read long-term memory
├─ invoke_agent Strands Agents                 10s
│  ├─ execute_event_loop_cycle                 4.4s
│  │  ├─ chat → chat global.zai.glm-5.3        4.0s        ← first model call, decides to retrieve
│  │  └─ kb_search → Bedrock Agent Runtime.Retrieve   444ms  ← retrieval from lab-unicorn-policies
│  └─ execute_event_loop_cycle                 5.8s
│     └─ chat → chat global.zai.glm-5.3        5.8s        ← writes the final answer (905 output tokens)
└─ Bedrock AgentCore.CreateEvent ×2            98–101ms    ← write this turn back to memory

Compare the chat and kb_search durations first. Here the two model calls total 9.8 seconds and the retrieval 0.4 seconds: the time goes into the model, not retrieval; if a tool span were clearly longer, you would look at retrieval or the gateway. The Span card to the right of the waterfall shows the first failed span, or the first model-category span when nothing failed (here chat); click any row to switch to it. Click the second chat global.zai.glm-5.3: the card shows Span chat global.zai.glm-5.3, Model global.zai.glm-5.3, Provider aws.bedrock, Finish reason end_turn, Starts at +5.5s, Duration 5.8s, Status UNSET · http 200, a Tokens section with Input 2, Output 905, Cache read / write 0 / 0, Est. cost ≈$0.005, and Attributes · 32 below (Show all expands the raw attributes). This span records no message content, so the Input · N messages / Output · N messages sections do not appear (frontend/src/v3/pages/observability/TraceView.tsx renders them only when the span carries messages).

About Input being 2: GLM-5.3 spans count the prompt as cache traffic — click the invoke_agent Strands Agents row and its card shows 13,118 cache-read and 15,749 cache-write tokens — and the model span reports only 2 non-cached input tokens. Almost every token figure in this chapter is therefore output tokens.

When system traces exist, the Traces tab shows a Show N system traces checkbox (the two-span InternalOperation health checks a managed Harness runtime emits). There were none in this lab's 24 hours, so the checkbox did not appear (frontend/src/v3/pages/observability/Lists.tsx shows it only when systemCount is above 0).

Telemetry is per endpoint

Every AgentCore endpoint writes its own log group (…-<endpoint>) and service name (….<endpoint>). In gated mode:

Traffic Endpoint Where you see it
Chat, public API (/v1/...), online evaluation, scheduled regression runs live The service name in the trace header's small line ends in .live
The release evaluation of a candidate (the Evaluate and Release chapters) candidate Service ends in .candidate

The rule the platform applies: a run pinned to an endpoint reads that endpoint; a gated agent reads live; everything else reads DEFAULT. The dashboards, online evaluation and insights therefore show the endpoint your users actually talk to, not an idle DEFAULT. In this lab only lab-service-assistant is on dual endpoints (service lab_service_assistant_434922.live); lab-policy-advisor never went through the gate and its traces carry the service harness_lab_policy_advisor.DEFAULT.

Expected result: the header's small line reads lab-service-assistant · … · lab_service_assistant_434922.live (the service ends in .live; the runtime suffix differs per environment); the waterfall has both chat global.zai.glm-5.3 and kb_search spans, and the Span card shows their tokens and estimated cost.

5. Put a number on tokens and cost (admin)

Sign in as admin (administrators see every module by default) and open rail Modules → Agent runtime → Spend & alerts (/v3/costs). Only administrators see this entry, and GET /api/costs is admin-only.

In the image: 1 tiles: Est. spend · 24h, Month to date, Tokens, Agents with traffic; 2 window 1h–30d; 3 By agent (the unnumbered box is the live endpoint of the current lab-service-assistant); 4 By person: Unattributed (API or evaluation) and developer; 5 the Alerts tab.

The Spend tab (switch between Spend / Alerts on the right of the page header):

  • The page opens with a watch summary; with no alert rule yet it reads "Nothing is watched yet — add a threshold to be told when spend, errors or latency move.", and All rules next to it jumps to the Alerts tab.
  • KPIs: Est. spend · 24h ("Estimate, from the price map"), Month to date, Tokens, Agents with traffic. Below them you switch the window (1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d), and Re-read bypasses the cache. In this lab, 24h: $1.18, month to date $1.32, 284,784 tokens, 9 agents.
  • By agent: attributed from the runtime service name on each span, one row per <runtime>.<endpoint> with estimated cost, Tokens and Model calls. The live endpoint of lab-service-assistant reads lab_service_assistant_434922.live · $0.12 · 22,408 · 36. The same runtime has two more rows: lab_service_assistant_434922.DEFAULT ($0.37 · 89,160 · 111, the calls before the Release chapter moved it onto dual endpoints, including the Evaluate chapter's dev run) and lab_service_assistant_434922.candidate ($0.24 · 42,582 · 98, the gate's evaluations of candidate versions). The other rows are the endpoints of lab-canary-sandbox, lab-legacy-agent (service lab_legacy_container_*) and lab-policy-advisor (harness_lab_policy_advisor.DEFAULT).
  • By person: console sessions joined to the person who opened them, with columns Person and Sessions. Here developer reads $0.20 over 14 sessions (section 1's conversations included).
  • Unattributed (API or evaluation): public API calls and evaluation runs have no console session, so they get their own row in the By person table (here $0.98 over 125 sessions).

The Alerts tab: an administrator can create a New rule whose What to watch is Error rate, p95 latency, Online quality or Spend this month, with an https Webhook (optional) (notified once when the rule goes from ok to firing). Rules are readable by every member and writable by administrators only. Still as admin, create one rule that mirrors criterion P2:

  1. Switch to Alerts on the right of the page header. The page shows four tiles, Firing, Close to the line, Unknown and Rules, and "No rules yet.". Click New rule.
  2. In the "New alert rule" dialog: What to watch p95 latency (hint: "95th percentile end-to-end latency, in milliseconds."); Name lab-p95-30s; Fire when above ms 30000; Window left at 24h (choices 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d); Webhook (optional) empty. Click Create.

In the image: 1 What to watch: p95 latency; 2 Name lab-p95-30s; 3 Fire when above ms: 30000; 4 Window stays 24h; 5 click Create (Webhook left empty).

  1. Expected result: the toast "Rule created", and a new lab-p95-30s card reading "p95 latency above 30000 ms · 24h", state Unknown and "not checked yet"; Unknown and Rules both become 1.
  2. Click Re-check now; the toast reads "Re-checked · 0 firing". The card turns OK with last value 20346 ms (the dashboard's P95 of 20s), detail p95 over 157 traces, and Unknown drops back to 0. Above 30000 ms the rule goes Firing, and with a webhook it notifies once on the change from ok to firing (backend/app/services/alerts.py).

In the image: 1 Re-check now; 2 the rule card: p95 latency above 30000 ms · 24h, OK after the check, last value 20346 ms, detail "p95 over 157 traces".

Leave the rule in place; section 2.2 of the Clean-up chapter deletes it.

6. Intent view: what are people asking

Back in the biz-owner window, click rail Modules → Agent evaluation → Intent view (/v3/intents). Leave the range on the right of the page header at 7 days (also: 1, 14, 30 days) and change the agent picker from All agents to lab-service-assistant.

How to read the page:

  • The intent view groups by each session's first message, so a session counts once: section 1's five-question session is grouped by "I bought Bluetooth earbuds on Unicorn Mall…", and the lab-policy-advisor session by "Can a flash-sale item…".
  • Tiles: Sessions, Intents, Unanswered, Most disliked intent.
  • Questions it could not answer: refusals, empty answers and errors; each row has Send to issue box and Open session.
  • What people asked: columns Intent, Sessions, Thumbs-down rate, Unanswered, and View N at the end of each row opens that group's sessions. Normally an AI model (global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5, backend/app/services/intents.py) names the intents in business language.

Expected result (measured in this lab, lab-service-assistant, 7 days, back 8.6 seconds after Regroup):

  • The page title "1 question went unanswered"; Sessions 8, Intents 5 (with "Grouped by an AI model from each session's first message."), Unanswered 1, Most disliked intent — (nobody has thumbed down yet).
  • Questions it could not answer has 1 row: "我下周去成都出差两晚，按我的习惯给点订机票和订酒店的建议。" from an earlier chapter, whose recorded answer is only "好的！先根据您的偏好帮您查一下相关政策，再给建议。", intent Flight and hotel booking advice, with Send to issue box and Open session.
  • What people asked has 5 rows (one observed set of names, with sessions): Earbuds return eligibility inquiry 4, Flight and hotel booking advice 1, Flight ticket refund calculation 1, Partial order refund calculation 1, Record personal travel habits 1. Section 1's English and Chinese sessions are all in Earbuds return eligibility inquiry, because each opens with the earbuds return (this lab ran the Chinese session twice); the fourth is an earbuds question from an earlier chapter.
  • The model decides both the group names and Unanswered afresh on every call: on top of the rules (empty answer, error, refusal wording) it also flags sessions whose answer did not actually answer the question (backend/app/services/intents.py). In this lab one grouping of the same 8 sessions on the zh page made 4 groups and counted 0 unanswered.
  • Switching the picker to lab-policy-advisor puts section 1's flash-sale session in Flash sale coupon stacking rules (one observed name, 2 sessions).

In the image: 1 agent picker set to lab-service-assistant; 2 Regroup; 3 tiles: Sessions 8, Intents 5 (grouped by an AI model from each session's first message), Unanswered 1; 4 Questions it could not answer: the Chengdu trip question; 5 What people asked: Earbuds return eligibility inquiry 4 and four groups of 1 (one observed set of names).

Under All agents (18 sessions in this lab) the grouping is AI too: after Regroup the four tiles show — first, and in this lab the result arrived after 10.1 seconds (8.6 seconds on the zh page). The result is cached on the server for 10 minutes, so reopening the page in that time shows the cached result straight away. One observed result: "3 questions went unanswered", Sessions 18, Intents 10, Unanswered 3. Group names move between calls: on the zh page the same earbuds sessions were named "蓝牙耳机七天无理由退货咨询" in the All agents call and "蓝牙耳机退货政策咨询" in the lab-service-assistant call.

This is one of the doors into the Feed back chapter: the business owner spots a problem here and works it in the issue box and admission queue.

7. Policy decision logs (admin)

In the Release chapter admin attached a policy engine to the shared launchpad-gw, wrote Cedar policies, collected evidence with Policy test and finally switched to ENFORCE. Still as admin, open rail Modules → Agent runtime → Governance (/v3/governance); on the Gateways tab, in the Policy decisions card (last 24h) the launchpad-gw row reads launchpad_gw_policy · ENFORCE, with Allowed 2 and Denied 5 in this lab; click Decisions on that row. It opens the gateway detail page hosted inside V3 (address /v2/governance?view=gateway&gateway=…&section=decisions), already on its Decisions section.

  • At the top: Time range (default Last 24 hours) and a Policy filter (default All).
  • KPI tiles, in order: Decisions, LOG_ONLY evidence ("what the cutover gate counts"), Allowed, Denied. In this lab: 7, 3, 2, 5.
  • Evidence breakdown (source: CloudWatch policy metrics) splits by operation, enforcement mode and policy. In this lab: By operation AuthorizeAction 2 allowed / 5 denied; By enforcement mode ENFORCE 2 / 2, LOG_ONLY 0 / 3; By policy unicorn_payout_admin_only-… 0 / 2, unicorn_tool_allowlist-… 2 / 0. The note below says the breakdowns are not a decomposition of the total (AWS publishes the policy dimension only for decisions that had a determining policy, and the tool dimension only for per-tool authorization), so the two By policy rows adding up to 4 rather than the 7 Decisions is expected.
  • Policy decisions rows come from Policy spans and are sampled. This lab shows "No per-decision rows (Policy spans) in this window" and "Gateway tracing is not configured (delivery_source_missing). Configure trace delivery for this Gateway, then generate new traffic; tracing is not retroactive.": the workshop template does not configure trace delivery for launchpad-gw; the counts above are unaffected.
  • With no decision at all in the window, the tiles read 0 and the page says "No policy decisions in this window." (frontend/src/v2/pages/governance/Decisions.tsx); widening Time range to Last 7 days brings back the Release chapter's policy tests. This lab had 7 decisions in 24 hours, so that did not occur.

The Audit section next to it is the gateway's immutable change log.

8. Drift watch: re-apply the standard on a schedule

A model can change under an agent without a line of code changing. A standard checked only at release time stops being a standard within weeks. The drift watch replays the golden set's regression split against live on a schedule and scores it with the same criteria table.

As developer open rail Modules → Agent evaluation → Standards, pick lab-service-assistant in the agent picker on the right of the page header, and click the Drift watch sub-tab (/v3/standards?agent=<id>&view=watch). From top to bottom the page shows Alerts, Pass rate against its baseline, Agent or judge?, Schedule and Scheduled runs.

In the image: 1 Alerts: "Nothing firing across the last 6 run(s)…" and "Too little history…"; 2 Pass rate against its baseline (Quality by default, "Baseline has 5 of the 8 points it needs."); 3 Agent or judge?: agent versions 2, 3, 4, 4 judges needing recalibration; 4 Schedule: Daily, 3, 1, 5, Enabled, On, next run 2026-10-11 03:00; 5 Scheduled runs: the unnumbered box is the 2bd991f6 regression row added by Run now.

Before you save a schedule, this lab's page reads: Alerts 0, "Nothing firing across the last 5 run(s), checked …"; Pass rate against its baseline notes "Baseline has 4 of the 8 points it needs."; the Schedule card is tagged Not scheduled and Run now is greyed out (it cannot be clicked without a schedule, frontend/src/v3/pages/standards/Watch.tsx); Scheduled runs already holds 5 rows, the dev, regression and holdout runs from the Evaluate and Release chapters (versions 2, 3, 4, criteria v1) — the table lists every run of this agent against this criteria table, not only scheduled ones.

Fill in the Schedule card:

Field Value Notes
How often Daily Weekly is the other option
At hour (UTC) 3 0–23
Repeats (k) 1 Above 1 the cost multiplies on every run
Cost ceiling (USD) 5 (the confirm amount set in the Roles chapter) A run estimated above it is skipped and reported, rather than spent
Enabled checked

Click Save at the bottom of the card ("Schedule saved"); the card's tag changes from Not scheduled to On and "Next run 2026-10-11 03:00" (the next 03:00 UTC) appears. Then click Run now next to it (the success toast is "Run started"); the line under the card becomes "Next run 2026-10-11 03:00 · Last run queued — run 2bd991f645b3". It still says "Last run queued" after the run finishes: last_status records only queued and skipped-for-cost, so read the outcome in Scheduled runs.

Saving the schedule pins the criteria table's currently published version to the watch. When the table later publishes a new version, come back and click Save again so the watch picks it up (the Feed back chapter relies on this).

In this lab the run (task watch regression 2026-10-10, 15 regression items, 4 evaluators) went from queued at 11:16:03 (UTC) to completed at 11:24:23, 8 min 20 s; mean scores Builtin.Correctness 0.93, unicorn_privacy_guard 0.93, unicorn_no_overpromise 0.87, unicorn_fee_check 0.80. Refresh and read:

  • Alerts: each family is judged its own way. Count (red-line violations, evaluation errors) uses an absolute threshold and Pages immediately; Score waits for a baseline of at least 8 points, otherwise it says "Too little history to judge a drop in: …"; Mix compares the intent distribution and names the component that moved (none in this lab). When nothing fires the page says so explicitly — "Nothing firing across the last N run(s), checked …" — because a dead monitor must not read as fourteen quiet days. Here: "Nothing firing across the last 6 run(s), checked 2026-10-10 11:25." and "Too little history to judge a drop in: Cognition, Quality, Responsibility. Nothing is claimed until the baseline is long enough."
  • Pass rate against its baseline: pick a dimension at the top right of the card (only dimensions with data are listed; Quality by default); the dashed line is the rolling median of preceding runs. Here the choices are Cognition, Quality and Responsibility, and the chart notes "Baseline has 5 of the 8 points it needs.".
  • Agent or judge?: a dip can be the agent getting worse or the judge changing its mind. It lists Agent versions in this window and Judges needing recalibration, and the table below shows, per judge criterion, whether it is Calibrated and its κ; a version change is highlighted in amber. Here: Agent versions in this window 2, 3, 4 (amber), Judges needing recalibration 4, and the table shows C1 Builtin.Correctness, Q1 unicorn_fee_check-… and S1 unicorn_privacy_guard-… as Never calibrated and S2 unicorn_no_overpromise-… as Found not aligned, κ 1.00 (the Evaluate chapter's calibration sample carried a single label, so κ is recorded as 1.00 by convention, and it was found not aligned).
  • Scheduled runs: time, split, agent version and criteria version per run; click a row to open the evaluation task detail.

Expected result: Schedule shows On; Scheduled runs ends with a new row 2bd991f6 · 2026-10-10 11:16 · regression · 4 · v1 (your run id and time differ); Alerts is 0.

Scheduled runs invoke the agent and evaluators every day and cost money. At the end of the workshop come back, uncheck Enabled and Save (the Cleanup chapter reminds you too).

9. Scorecard and decision history

Scorecard (business owner)

In the biz-owner window open Standards, pick lab-service-assistant in the page header; the default sub-tab is Scorecard (view=scorecard). It is the page a business owner reads (the readings below are from after the section 8 run):

  • Needs attention: what needs a person comes first. Here 2 items, both waiting: "4 judge criteria are uncalibrated and only observe" (link Calibration) and "1 waiver(s) open" (link Release gate).
  • Are we meeting the standard we signed: tiles Standard v1 (signer biz-owner), Last gate PASS ("Released · 2026-10-10 08:30"), Uncalibrated judges 4 ("These criteria are recorded but do not block."), Alerts firing 0 ("Nothing firing"). Then the five dimension tiles: Cognition 93.3%, Quality 80.0%, Responsibility 90.0% (all three read "Standard —" and "0 of N gates in force": their criteria are uncalibrated judges that only observe); Cost 798 in red ("Tokens per session <= 500 · n = 15"; K1 went live on a waiver); Performance 11,821 (two lines, "Latency P95 (ms) <= 60,000 · n = 15" and "<= 30,000 · n = 15", for P1 and P2). n = 15 shows the tiles read the latest run, the section 8 drift-watch run (before it, this lab read Cognition 88.9%, Quality 55.6%, Responsibility 66.7%, Cost 1,060 and Performance 8,162 with n = 9, from the release holdout run). A dimension nobody wrote a criterion for would say "Not applicable — nobody wrote a criterion here"; every dimension of this criteria table has criteria, so it does not appear.
  • The Release card: Live 4, Endpoints live / candidate endpoints, Last run 2026-10-10 11:16 (the section 8 drift-watch run).
  • What the standard still owes: C1, Q1, S1 as Uncalibrated judges · Never calibrated, S2 as Uncalibrated judges · Found not aligned (the Evaluate chapter's calibration came out not aligned, and not aligned does not count as calibrated), and K1 as Live waivers · biz-owner · 2026-10-24.
  • Coverage: criteria × case tier (Known good / Known bad / Ambiguous / Adversarial / Items); here P1, P2 and K1 have 48 items each and S1 only 5 adversarial items.

In the image: 1 Needs attention: "4 judge criteria are uncalibrated and only observe", "1 waiver(s) open"; 2 Standard v1 (biz-owner), Last gate PASS, Uncalibrated judges 4, Alerts firing 0; 3 the five dimensions: Cognition 93.3%, Quality 80.0%, Responsibility 90.0%, Cost 798, Performance 11,821 (after the drift-watch run, n = 15); 4 Release (live 4, live / candidate endpoints) and What the standard still owes (C1, Q1, S1, S2 and waiver K1).

Decision history (admin)

Switch to the Decision history sub-tab (view=audit). It is meant to answer who signed the standard, who admitted a sample, who approved a waiver and who released; filter above the table by All decisions / Criteria / Golden set / Calibration / Releases / Waivers; the columns are When, Who, What, On.

Its API, GET /api/audit, is admin-only: for biz-owner the table area says "Administrator access is required for this action." (the API returns 403 auth.forbidden). Read it in the admin window.

The page only shows records whose On contains the current agent's id, and the Standards page header always has an agent selected, so only records about the agent itself appear. In this lab admin sees 3 rows:

When Who What On
2026-10-10 08:04:38 release-ops release.rollback 0fda9dcf…
2026-10-10 07:58:38 developer waiver.request 0fda9dcf…:K1
2026-10-10 07:00:41 release-ops release.migrate_live 0fda9dcf…

Signing the criteria, curating the golden set, calibrating, approving a waiver, and evaluating and signing a release act on the ids of the criteria table, the golden set, the labelling task, the waiver and the release record, so they do not appear in this table. For the full history, admin opens <ConsoleUrl>/api/audit?limit=50 in the browser and reads the raw JSON (field events). In this lab there are 12 events and, newest first, every step of the chain is there: release.sign (release-ops, release record e2a2dc46… for v4), release.evaluate (developer, v4), release.rollback (release-ops), release.sign (release-ops, release record b2bc2f9b… for v3), waiver.approve (release-ops, waiver 25061f02…), waiver.request (developer), calibration.not_aligned (biz-owner, the S2 decision), release.evaluate (developer, v3), release.migrate_live (release-ops), golden.seed (biz-owner, 48816caa5d80), criteria.sign (biz-owner, 1c8eab7b1a314d35:v1), release_policy.update (admin, default). Saving the schedule and Run now in section 8 write no decision record.

In the image: 1 the agent picked in the page header, lab-service-assistant; 2 the Decision history sub-tab; 3 filters All decisions / Criteria / Golden set / Calibration / Releases / Waivers; 4 the table: release.rollback, waiver.request, release.migrate_live.

Checklist

  • The observability dashboard's Sessions and Tokens show data; Tools has kb_search and …___Retrieve
  • A session detail shows the conversation replay and Traces in this session
  • The waterfall shows chat global.zai.glm-5.3 and kb_search spans with tokens and estimated cost
  • developer scored a session once with Score now (Builtin.Helpfulness + unicorn_privacy_guard)
  • The service name in the trace header ends in .live (production traffic in gated mode)
  • admin sees estimated spend by agent and by person in Spend & alerts and created the alert rule lab-p95-30s
  • Intent view with lab-service-assistant picked is grouped by the AI, and section 1's sessions are in the earbuds-return group
  • The Drift watch of lab-service-assistant is scheduled and one regression run completed
  • biz-owner reads the Scorecard; admin reads the Decision history and the full record at /api/audit

Troubleshooting

Symptom Cause Fix
Every observability view is empty CloudWatch Transaction Search is not enabled Re-check it in the Setup chapter
No trace right after chatting The spans have not landed yet (all visible within 2.5 minutes in this lab) Wait, then Refresh
Numbers change only after a while 60-second cache Refresh bypasses it
Cost shows — Model missing from the price map Administrator clicks Update prices
Score now: "No span records found for this session in the selected time range yet." Spans not landed yet, or the range is too narrow Widen the range and retry
A session or trace detail says "This session was not found in the selected range." / "This trace …" The range starts after the session Go back to the list, widen the range to 7D and open it again
The trace service ends in .DEFAULT The agent is not on gated live / candidate endpoints Check the release policy is gated and the release stage finished
Drift watch Run now is greyed out The schedule was never saved (the console disables the button without a schedule; calling the API directly returns watch.not_configured) Click Save first
watch.over_cost_ceiling Estimate above the Cost ceiling Raise the ceiling or lower Repeats
watch.no_golden / watch.empty_split No golden set serves the criteria, or the regression split has no active items Check the golden set's criteria link and regression split (the Evaluate chapter; regression should hold 15 items)
biz-owner gets a permission error on Decision history GET /api/audit is admin-only Use admin
Online evaluation or Governance is missing from the rail In a fresh window a member account shows the everyday modules only Click Show every module at the bottom of Modules
Intent view tiles stay at — after Regroup The AI grouping has not returned yet (in this lab 10.1 s for All agents, 8.6 s for lab-service-assistant) Wait for it, or pick a specific agent; if the AI call fails the page shows the amber notice "The AI grouping was unavailable…" and falls back to mechanical grouping (backend/app/services/intents.py)
Decision history lacks criteria.sign and similar records The table only shows records about the current agent Open <ConsoleUrl>/api/audit?limit=50 as admin
